thesis: The index is the macro, and the macro has a dated binary in it: the FOMC on 15-16 Sep with futures pricing a hike at 58-66% after August payrolls came in at +162k against +53k expected. Buying beta ten days before a coin-flip rate decision, with the 10-year near 4.8% and index concentration at record levels, is paying the spread for someone else's opinion. Flat until the decision is on the tape.
bull_case: The trend has not broken: packet close 770.19 above SMA50 above SMA200, 3m momentum +4.7%, and the S&P 500 finished 7,718.60 on Fri 4 Sep, close to its highs. Realised volatility is low - ATR 0.7%, the calmest in the whole signal table. The jobs number that spooked rates was a strong number: +162k with unemployment steady at 4.1% is an economy that is not rolling over, and earnings from MSFT, AMZN and NVDA this cycle were genuinely good. Waller said on 3 Sep he was inclined to support holding at 3.5-3.75%, so the hike is not settled.
bear_case: Yields are doing the damage: the 2-year hit its highest since January 2025 and the 10-year moved to ~4.8% on the 4 Sep payrolls print, and stocks fell on the day. Energy is re-accelerating inflation - renewed fighting in Iran has European gas futures at a three-year high and oil near $100 (Bloomberg, 2 Sep 2026). Index concentration is the worst part: AI-linked names are roughly 40-45% of S&P 500 market cap, so SPY is no longer the diversifier it is bought as - it is a leveraged AI bet with an index label. September seasonality is the weakest month of the year. RSI 48 and a +0.40 score say the index is drifting, not trending.
catalysts: 15-16 Sep 2026 FOMC decision and dot plot
August CPI print ahead of the FOMC
risks: A hawkish hike on 16 Sep with the 10-year through 5%
AI concentration means an AI drawdown is an index drawdown
Energy-driven inflation re-acceleration from the Iran conflict
invalidation: Flips to long on a weekly close above 790 (S&P ~7,900, new highs) after the 16 Sep FOMC; the risk case confirms on a close below 740 (S&P ~7,400), which breaks the SMA50 and the summer range.
